Selected case studies

Three ways the work already behaves like UX.

These are product and interaction case studies, not retroactive claims that every project was a formal user-research study.

CASE 01 · INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE

ECOSTATE GripCube

7 · 6 · 63
visitor-first districts · semantic lenses · seeded public routes

A large estate needed a usable public front door without flattening its underlying structure. The solution separated major rooms from inspection lenses, then tested the rendered route across mobile and desktop.

EvidenceCorrected render QA: mobile + desktop 2/2 PASS.
UX signalInformation architecture, navigation grammar, error attribution and iterative QA.
BoundaryOwner-device visual/touch Ding remained separately gated at the recorded integration stage.
What changed?

The design stopped forcing six cube faces to carry seven public districts. Horizontal movement became major-room travel; cube rotation became lens/orientation; local routes stayed local. Different navigation meanings stopped overwriting each other.

CASE 02 · ADAPTIVE LEARNING UX

Teaching / Learning Engine

4 doors
Quick · Probe · Make · Read contact modes

Designed around the idea that a learner should not be reduced to one current route. The system supports hints, recovery, adaptive rebalance, co-op without ranking people and human override.

EvidenceImplemented engine structure carries learner lanes, hints, recovery, trace, adaptive suggestions and co-op.
UX signalChoice architecture, progressive assistance, personalisation and recovery-oriented interaction.
BoundaryHuman/parent choice remains governing; suggestion is not diagnosis.
Why it matters?

The same learner can need a different door at a different moment. The interface therefore treats difficulty as route information rather than identity.

CASE 03 · INTERACTION QA

BRAIDGE

94 / 0
static controls accounted for · unbound controls

An interaction-heavy body required the distinction between automated confidence and real-device acceptance. Desktop/mobile viewports, gesture routes, replay, resume, export and lineage were tested, while Android haptics stayed outside the automated crown.

Evidence390×844, 360×800 and 1366×768 QA passed; 94 controls accounted for.
UX signalResponsive interaction, gesture testing, state recovery and acceptance criteria.
BoundaryReal downloaded-file persistence / Android haptics remained owner-device tests at v1.4.
What is the research habit?

Do not let a test environment silently stand in for the user environment. The test route records exactly which surface earned which claim.

Working method

Observe first. Crown later.

My default research/product loop is simple enough to explain and strict enough to stop a convenient story replacing the contact.

01
ObserveWhat actually happened? Capture contact before explanation.
02
SeparateDistinguish trace, assumption, interpretation and desired outcome.
03
LocateFind the route, state, interface or condition where mismatch appears.
04
ChangeAlter the smallest layer that plausibly explains the friction.
05
RetestRepeat on the relevant surface rather than assuming the fix travelled.
06
BoundState what the evidence earns — and what it does not.

Research posture: contact can correct the model. A neat explanation does not outrank what actually happened.

Authorship / tooling disclosure

What is mine, what is assisted, what is proved.

My contribution

Concept, product direction, interaction logic, research/test criteria, correction decisions, claim boundaries and overall system design.

AI-assisted work

Retrieval, implementation, prototyping, drafting, code generation and testing assistance are used where useful. I do not present assisted implementation as solitary hand-coding.

Proof discipline

Build success, automated QA, owner-device contact and public deployment are treated as different evidence classes. A pass in one does not silently become a pass in all.

Why say this? Because the useful capability is not pretending tools do not exist. It is directing them, testing the output, diagnosing failures and knowing what the result actually proves.
